title: Finiteness of the dimension of a finite type scheme
statement:
Let $K$ be a field and $X$ a scheme of finite type over $K$.
Then $\kundim X<\infty$.

proof.text: For every point x∈X, the local-dimension node gives finiteness of dim O_{X,x}, and the residue-field node gives finiteness of trdeg_K κ(x). Applying the unit-mandated dimension formula [lem-kun-dimension-formula] yields kundim_x X < ∞. If X is empty, the conclusion is immediate.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph; dimension-at-a-point argument via lem-kun-dimension-formula

proof.text: By the definition of kundim as the supremum of lengths of strict chains, the global dimension is the supremum of the finite dimensions at points (for each irreducible component, a generic point realizes its component dimension; every chain is contained in a component).

source.place: Proof, second paragraph; supremum over point dimensions

proof.text: The structure morphism X→Spec K is of finite type. Since K is Noetherian, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes X Noetherian, and [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-irreducible-components] gives finitely many irreducible components.
The supremum in Step 2 is therefore a maximum of finitely many finite component dimensions, hence finite; this is the finite-component maximum argument and also covers the empty scheme.
